title: EIF framework lock (.eif/framework.lock.yaml) - EIF-managed, never hand-edited
description: Exact provenance of the materialized instance runtime: which framework source produced it (a git commit, an installed package, or an asserted source-bundle export - see framework.source_type), whether it was dirty, the exact bundle file hashes, which adapter entrypoint was generated, and when. Fully regenerated by scripts/eif_init.py on every init/upgrade - a routine upgrade rewrites this file completely and never touches the user-owned .eif/config.yaml. See docs/architecture/instance-contract.md.

source_type.description: Discriminates which of the top-level `git` / `package` / `source_bundle` objects carries this instance's actual provenance - see the sibling `if`/`then` conditions below. Exactly one is ever required, never a fake stand-in for another (e.g. an installed-package source never invents a git-shaped commit SHA).

git.description: Present when framework.source_type is 'git': a real, git-verified (or explicitly --framework-ref-asserted) commit of a git checkout.

commit_sha.description: Real framework git commit this instance was generated from - always a full 40-hex SHA, never a placeholder or branch name.

dirty.description: True if --framework-root's working tree had uncommitted changes when this bundle was materialized. See --allow-dirty in eif_init.py.

package.description: Present when framework.source_type is 'installed-package': the eifctl console-script was generated from an installed Python distribution, not a framework git checkout. There is no git commit to report for this case - it is not fabricated as one.

distribution.description: The installed package's distribution name (importlib.metadata terms), e.g. 'engineering-intelligence-framework'.

python_version.description: 'major.minor.micro' of the interpreter that ran `eifctl init`.

wheel_sha256.description: sha256 of the actual installed wheel/archive file, read from the distribution's direct_url.json (archive_info.hash) when present. Omitted - never fabricated - when the install method does not record it (e.g. an editable/local-directory install).

resource_manifest_digest.description: Combined digest over every file actually present in the installed package's bundled resources/ tree right now (see scripts/sync_package_sources.py), sorted (relative path, sha256) pairs. Always computable at generation time - unlike wheel_sha256, never optional. `eifctl doctor` recomputes this against the currently-installed resources/ tree to detect a modified/corrupted install.

source_bundle.description: Present when framework.source_type is 'source-bundle': --framework-root is neither a git checkout nor an installed eifctl package (e.g. a plain tarball/zip export) and the caller explicitly asserted an identifier via --framework-ref. Trustworthy only as far as whoever passed that flag - kept structurally separate from both `git` (a real git-verified commit) and `package` (real installed-distribution metadata) so neither is ever confused with an unverified assertion.

asserted_ref.description: The identifier supplied via --framework-ref. Not required to look like a git SHA - it is whatever the caller asserts identifies this bundle.

dirty.description: The actually-detected dirty state of --framework-root if it happens to be a git repo underneath (rare for a genuine source-bundle export); false when there is nothing to detect. Never forced false just because the ref itself is asserted rather than verified.

effective_root_markers.description: For an adapter with a registered root_marker_option_key (Codex: project_root_markers) - the exact marker list actually used to resolve the project root when this instance was last generated, whether that came from adapter.options.<adapter> or the adapter's own documented default. An empty array is a real, valid value (root detection explicitly disabled), distinct from the key being absent (no such adapter concept). eif_verify_runtime.py's doctor recomputes the CURRENT effective list and fails if it no longer matches - a hand-edited config.yaml changing this value with no re-run is exactly the kind of drift this is meant to catch.

manifest.description: Every file eif_init.py's BUNDLE_SCRIPTS/BUNDLE_TREES copied FROM THE FRAMEWORK SOURCE, hashed before copying. Scope is precise, not 'everything under the bundle path': files written into the bundle AFTER staging (README.md) and interpreter-generated files (__pycache__/) are intentionally outside this list - see eif_verify_runtime.py's KNOWN_UNMANIFESTED_* classification, which reports any OTHER unlisted file as a real integrity concern rather than ignoring it.

digest.description: Combined hash over the sorted manifest - lets a consumer verify the whole bundle in one comparison without re-hashing every file.

knowledge_index.description: Provenance of the EIF-managed knowledge index, present only when eif_init.py actually created or regenerated one this run (knowledge.managed: true and a knowledge root exists) - absent entirely when the index was skipped. Lets eif_verify_runtime.py detect drift: a hand-edited index file (hash mismatch) or one that has silently lost its ownership marker.
